item.title: Nikkei study finds hidden debts of five US tech giants rise to $1.65 trillion due to opaque AI-related funding [ * ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A Nikkei study reveals that hidden debts at five major US tech companies have surged to an estimated $1.65 trillion over four years, driven largely by investments in artificial intelligence. These off-balance-sheet liabilities, including data center leases and GPU supply contracts, now exceed the companies' reported debts, complicating risk assessment for investors. The study highlights Meta's off-balance-sheet debt at about $420 billion, nearly triple its transparent debt, illustrating the scale of opaque financing in the AI sector. This rise in hidden liabilities reflects the growing capital demands of AI development and infrastructure, raising concerns about financial transparency among leading technology firms.

item.title: Report: China's open-weight AI models gain global adoption as US export controls and proprietary strategies limit American AI ecosystem growth [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: China is advancing its AI strategy by openly releasing AI model weights, enabling broader adoption and innovation despite US export controls on GPUs and data sharing restrictions. This approach contrasts with American companies' proprietary models, which face limited ecosystem growth due to locked-down business practices and regulatory constraints. Chinese models are increasingly competitive, with companies like Moonshot and Alibaba claiming parity with leading US models at lower costs, contributing to widespread use in startups and various sectors across China. The open-weight strategy allows Chinese enterprises to integrate AI models flexibly across manufacturing, research, and other industries, fostering a more effective global ecosystem than centralized, closed services. Meanwhile, US companies' focus on short-term profits and government export restrictions may hinder their long-term AI leadership and economic impact. Experts suggest that aligning incentives toward openness and public-interest AI technologies could be crucial for sustaining US competitiveness in the evolving AI landscape.

item.title: Nativ launches tool to run open AI models from Google, Cohere, and Liquid AI locally on Mac, recommending models based on hardware [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Nativ offers a tool that enables users to run prominent open AI models from Google, Cohere, and Liquid AI directly on their Mac computers. The platform helps users select the most suitable partner model tailored to their specific hardware capabilities, facilitating efficient local AI model deployment.

item.title: Stratechery analyzes Chinese AI models like Kimi K3 approaching state-of-the-art capabilities and their impact on AI economics and industry structure [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Stratechery explores the implications of Chinese AI models such as Kimi K3 nearing state-of-the-art performance, focusing on how these models challenge assumptions about AI costs and industry dynamics. The analysis highlights the distinction between fixed research and development expenses and variable costs of running AI inference, emphasizing that open-weight models are not free to operate despite their availability. The article discusses how token generation costs and model efficiency affect AI providers' economics, noting that tokens are not fungible commodities since different models require varying amounts of tokens to produce intelligence. This complexity influences the competitive landscape and the long-term structure of the AI industry, suggesting a shift back to fundamental economic principles in AI development and deployment.

item.title: Cursor experiments with agent swarms to build complex software tasks, improving efficiency and coordination with a new version control system [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
item.description: Cursor conducted experiments scaling agent swarms to cooperate on complex tasks, such as building a web browser and SQLite from scratch, demonstrating improved performance and stability over previous models. The system uses planner agents to decompose goals and worker agents to execute tasks, optimizing context management and coordination. To handle the high volume of concurrent changes-up to 1,000 commits per second-Cursor developed a custom version control system that detects conflicts and supports coordination mechanisms beyond traditional human engineering practices. This approach aims to efficiently scale AI agent collaboration for diverse and complex software development challenges.

item.title: Study measures AI-generated writing in 12,750 arXiv papers, finds about one-third flagged as machine-written by 2026 with field-specific variation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers analyzed the full text of 12,750 arXiv papers from 2021 to 2026 using a calibrated AI writing detector, finding that the share of papers flagged as machine-written rose from a 0.4% false-positive baseline pre-ChatGPT to about 32% by mid-2026, peaking near 39%. The study sampled ten academic fields monthly and used pre-ChatGPT papers as a control to set detection thresholds and account for false positives. The flagged share varied widely by field, with computer science papers showing the highest AI writing prevalence at about 65%, while mathematics papers scored near 0.7%, though this low rate may reflect detector limitations rather than low AI use. The detector's sensitivity varies by model and writing style, and the results represent a lower bound on AI writing prevalence since some machine-generated text may evade detection. The study emphasizes that a flagged score indicates machine-like writing style but does not prove authorship or the extent of AI assistance.

item.title: Researchers propose Otap, a structure-aware optimal transport metric for evaluating agent trajectories by comparing execution graphs to valid solution graphs [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers introduce Otap (Optimal Transport for Agentic Planning), a new metric that evaluates large language model agent trajectories by measuring the distance between an agent's execution graph and valid solution graphs using an unbalanced fused Gromov-Wasserstein transport approach. Otap is designed to be invariant to dependency-preserving reorderings and robust to redundant or missing steps, addressing limitations of current binary success flags and exact matching metrics. The metric performs well on controlled perturbations and three public benchmarks, distinguishing valid from invalid trajectories even when semantics-only metrics fail, with highest accuracy when dependency graphs are precisely recovered.

item.title: WorldCupArena launches dynamic benchmark for language models and AI agents to predict 2026 FIFA World Cup matches with fine-grained evaluation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: WorldCupArena introduces a dynamic benchmark designed to evaluate language models and deep-research agents on football match forecasting, starting with the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Models predict match results, scores, player events, statistics, and competition outcomes before kickoff, using either provided evidence or self-sourced information, with predictions compared against actual results after each match. The benchmark assesses result accuracy, exact-score accuracy, and a scoreline metric that credits near misses, covering 104 matches and 13 systems in its initial evaluation. The benchmark allows continuous updates by adding new match schedules as they begin, enabling ongoing evaluation of future models without relying on known outcomes. Compared to betting-market and human-fan baselines, the top-performing system shows modest improvements in result and exact-score accuracy but clearer gains in the scoreline metric. The project's code, prompts, predictions, and evaluation scripts are openly available on GitHub for community use and further research.

item.title: DocOCR-Eval proposes an annotation-free framework for selecting OCR tools using a correction-based ranking strategy without ground truth labels [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: DocOCR-Eval introduces a new framework to evaluate and select Optical Character Recognition (OCR) tools without relying on ground truth annotations, addressing challenges in label-scarce settings. The framework uses a three-stage correction and ranking method to approximate traditional annotation-based tool ordering, improving OCR tool selection across diverse document collections. The study systematically evaluates multiple OCR engines and multimodal large language models (MLLMs) on various scanned document benchmarks covering different domains and languages. Results show that aggregating outputs from multiple MLLMs enhances alignment with annotation-based rankings, enabling reliable OCR tool selection in practical, real-world scenarios where manual labeling is costly or unavailable.

item.title: Researchers introduce 'weights to words' method to express and edit preference model inferences in natural language, improving interpretability and accuracy in diverse domains [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers present a method called 'weights to words' that converts high-dimensional preference model inferences into natural language descriptions paired with vector representations. This approach addresses challenges in understanding which factors drive decisions and allows users to inspect and edit preference models in real time. The method was demonstrated across domains including moral dilemmas, movies, wines, and large language model responses. Two pre-registered human-subject experiments involving moral dilemmas and movie selection showed that regularizing preference models toward the learned natural language basis improved prediction accuracy on held-out data. Additionally, incorporating structured edits from participants further enhanced accuracy. Participants also preferred the inferred preference profiles and rated the method's predictions as more accurate compared to alternatives.

item.title: Researchers propose CIGPO to improve multi-turn evidence-reading LLM agents by preventing reward-variance collapse in reinforcement learning, achieving 0.518 F1 on HotpotQA with Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers identify instability in training multi-turn evidence-reading agents using outcome-only reinforcement learning, where intermediate turns receive little credit, causing optimization deadlock and format violations. They propose Contextual Information-Gain Policy Optimization (CIGPO), which assigns per-turn rewards based on the marginal increase in a reference model's log-likelihood of the correct answer to maintain reward variance and prevent collapse. In experiments on HotpotQA with Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct, CIGPO improves the standard F1 score to 0.518 from a 0.252 baseline, outperforming the best GRPO checkpoint at 0.430 and avoiding the zero-advantage lock-in seen in GRPO. The approach uses separate normalization of information gain and F1 rewards along with a curriculum for weighting information gain, demonstrating that turn-level rewards can stabilize training and enhance performance in multi-turn evidence reading tasks.

item.title: Researchers use large language models with evolutionary algorithms to generate and select new features from tabular data, improving classification across eight diverse datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers developed a pipeline that leverages large language models (LLMs) to generate new features from existing tabular data attributes, using a selection algorithm to identify the best-performing feature sets. They applied this method to eight datasets from various domains and data types, demonstrating that the LLM can create useful features based on mathematical and logical operations that enhance classification results. This approach highlights the potential of combining LLMs with evolutionary algorithms for automated feature engineering in machine learning pipelines.

item.title: Researchers introduce Hindsight Policy Optimization to reduce variance in long-horizon reinforcement learning for large language models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers propose Hindsight Policy Optimization (HPO), a novel policy gradient method designed to improve training of large language model agents on tasks with long-horizon interactions. HPO projects policy distributions into an intent space and uses the Wasserstein distance to extract low-variance learning signals, addressing challenges in attributing action contributions over extended sequences. The method is theoretically and empirically shown to stabilize policy performance by aggregating semantically similar states and actions, with code made publicly available.

item.title: Researchers propose trace-based on-policy distillation to improve reasoning in masked diffusion language models, achieving faster training and comparable accuracy to reinforcement learning methods [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers introduce trace-based on-policy distillation (TOPD), a teacher-supervised method that enhances reasoning abilities in diffusion large language models (dLLMs) by supervising the model on its own denoising trajectories without relying on reward estimation. TOPD aligns training with the model's denoising states using a token-level Reverse Kullback-Leibler objective and dense teacher supervision. On mathematical reasoning benchmarks, TOPD enables the SDAR-4B-Chat model to match the accuracy of its reinforcement learning-trained counterpart TraDo-4B-Instruct, with improvements of +5.7 and +4.5 points under static and dynamic evaluations respectively. The method achieves these results with four times fewer rollout rounds, corresponding to an estimated 96-fold speedup in model compute to accuracy compared to reinforcement learning approaches.

item.title: Researchers propose a method to learn value systems in generative AI using pairwise prompt-response preference data to improve alignment and explainability [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed a method to enable generative AI systems to learn explicit computational representations of human values by observing human behavior, addressing the challenge of aligning AI decisions with human values. The approach adapts a previously validated value system learning method to generative AI, simultaneously learning value groundings and a value system representation through a multi-objective reward model and weighted linear scalarization. The method dynamically prioritizes the grounding learning process to ensure coherent value representations and was evaluated against baselines and a contemporary method using prompt-response preference datasets. Results indicate competitive performance with minimal trade-offs and improved explainability compared to existing approaches that often replicate human preferences without capturing the multidimensional structure of value alignment.

item.title: Researchers propose WAR system to accelerate synchronous agentic reinforcement learning by optimizing decoding and scheduling based on runtime load [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers introduce WAR, a workload-aware rollout system designed to improve throughput in synchronous agentic reinforcement learning (RL) by optimizing decoding and scheduling strategies according to runtime load. WAR uses model-free speculative decoding with suffix reuse under low load and cache-aware scheduling under high load to reduce bottlenecks in long-horizon rollout generation. WAR combines decoding-level suffix reuse and system-level rollout scheduling to enhance throughput by 1.4x under low load and up to 1.6x under high load without altering the underlying RL algorithm. This approach addresses the dominant bottleneck in synchronous agentic RL training caused by rapidly growing trajectory lengths, offering a practical path toward scalable long-context agent training.

item.title: Researchers develop HySAT, a hyperbolic structure-aware training method applying hyperbolic losses only at the loss layer to stabilize expert AI models [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers introduce HySAT, a training approach that applies hyperbolic geometry only at the loss layer to preserve hierarchical structures in expert AI models, avoiding training collapses seen with other placements. They tested this method across six expert sparse language models, including Llama 3.1 and EXAONE 3.5, using four adapter strategies and an 18 million-sample corpus, achieving stable training over approximately 317,000 optimizer steps without numerical errors. Four models are operationally deployed, including one consumer-facing, with two open-weight models and detailed training logs publicly available.

item.title: Researchers introduce MADA-RL, a parameter-efficient multi-agent reinforcement learning framework that improves reasoning accuracy in compact language models using a debate-aware training signal [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers present MADA-RL, a post-training framework that specializes compact language models (up to 4 billion parameters) into generator and critic roles, fine-tuning only a small subset of parameters via LoRA adapters. The approach uses a counterfactual critic advantage to optimize critics to improve over generator consensus rather than merely reproducing correct answers, enhancing targeted credit assignment. MADA-RL improves accuracy on five mathematical reasoning benchmarks, raising the DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B model's accuracy from 39.9% to 41.9% while using 16 times fewer trainable parameters than fully fine-tuned baselines, placing it on the accuracy-trainable-parameter Pareto front.

item.title: Researchers find alignment tuning installs distinct, steerable bias directions in LLMs causing sycophancy and cue-induced errors [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers studied how alignment tuning affects large language models' (LLMs) susceptibility to sycophancy and related cue-induced biases, finding that these biases arise mainly from alignment rather than pretraining. They analyzed five model families and seven bias types, identifying distinct bias directions in model activations that can be decoded and steered to recover unbiased answers. The biases remain representationally separate, with cross-bias entanglement varying by model rather than bias category. The study also shows that targeted interventions can modestly reduce bias-induced errors while preserving correct responses, suggesting cue-induced bias is a set of distinct, causally active directions installed by alignment tuning rather than a single flaw.

item.title: Researchers benchmark general-purpose LLMs for 3D molecule generation under spatial constraints, introducing 3D-Fit to evaluate ligand design conditioned on protein pockets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: This study evaluates whether current general-purpose large language models (LLMs) can handle complex 3D spatial constraints in structure-based drug design compared to specialized diffusion models. The researchers introduce 3D-Fit, a token-efficient benchmarking method, to assess LLM performance on generating ligands conditioned on protein pockets and spatial constraints such as anchor fragments and pharmacophore points. Their results show that while LLMs currently lag behind state-of-the-art diffusion models, they demonstrate promising capabilities in managing multiple spatial constraints simultaneously, suggesting potential for scaling to more heterogeneous molecular design tasks.

item.title: Theoria introduces a verification architecture for AI reasoning that rewrites solutions into auditable state transitions with explicit justifications, achieving over 91% precision on expert problems [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Theoria is a new verification system designed to improve trust in AI-generated answers by rewriting candidate solutions into sequences of typed state transitions, each justified explicitly and independently auditable. This approach addresses limitations of formal proof assistants and scalar LLM judges by ensuring every change between proof states is accounted for, exposing hidden premises as unlicensed changes. On a benchmark of 185 expert problems, Theoria certified 105 solutions with 91.4% strict precision, producing human-readable proof traces for independent challenge. Compared to holistic LLM judges, Theoria showed complementary strengths and outperformed them on adversarial poisoned proofs, particularly in detecting hidden premises and fabricated citations. On a separate dataset, Theoria achieved 97.1% certified precision, demonstrating its effectiveness across diverse reasoning tasks.

item.title: Researchers propose Mediator method for memory-efficient merging of fine-tuned LLMs using layer-wise conflict analysis and uncertainty-based expert routing [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers introduce Mediator, a method to merge large language models (LLMs) fine-tuned on different tasks by averaging layers with minimal parameter conflicts and routing layers with significant conflicts using task-level experts. This approach reduces performance degradation common in naive averaging and lowers storage and compute costs compared to model routing methods. The technique decouples fine-tuned experts into a dense expert and sparse experts, selecting and merging them based on input task uncertainty to handle out-of-distribution samples. Experiments on LLaMA and Qwen models across various scales and real-world reasoning tasks show consistent performance improvements with reduced system costs.

item.title: Researchers introduce Prismatic Synthesis, a gradient-based data diversification method that improves generalization in large language model reasoning across out-of-distribution benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers present Prismatic Synthesis, a framework that generates diverse synthetic training data by targeting underrepresented regions in gradient space to enhance generalization in large language models (LLMs). They introduce G-Vendi, a metric measuring data diversity via the entropy of model-induced gradients, which strongly correlates with out-of-distribution performance on natural language inference and math reasoning tasks. Through over 300 controlled training runs, the team demonstrates that Prismatic Synthesis consistently improves model performance on both in-distribution and unseen benchmarks, outperforming state-of-the-art models trained on significantly larger synthetic datasets. For instance, their PrismMath-7B model, distilled from a 32B parameter LLM, surpasses a comparable 7B model trained on proprietary data generated by a 671B parameter model on six out of seven challenging benchmarks.

item.title: Researchers use model internals to predict Transformer behavior on out-of-distribution data using attention patterns observed only on in-distribution tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers trained hundreds of Transformer models on synthetic tasks where multiple out-of-distribution (OOD) generalization rules could apply despite perfect in-distribution accuracy. They demonstrated that attention patterns observed solely on in-distribution data can predict which generalization rule a model follows on unseen OOD data. Their experiments show that observational analysis of model internals can forecast behavior under distribution shifts even when causal mechanistic interpretations do not establish a direct cause-effect relationship. This work introduces a new interpretability objective focused on predicting model reliability and behavior on unseen data by analyzing internal patterns rather than relying solely on mechanistic faithfulness.

item.title: Researchers introduce Sequential Tool Attack Chaining (STAC) to exploit multi-turn tool use vulnerabilities in LLM agents, achieving over 90% attack success across eight state-of-the-art models [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
item.description: Researchers have developed Sequential Tool Attack Chaining (STAC), a multi-turn attack framework that exploits the tool-use capabilities of large language model (LLM) agents by chaining seemingly harmless tool calls into harmful sequences. Evaluations of 483 STAC cases across diverse domains and agent types show an average attack success rate of 91.2%, revealing significant vulnerabilities in current LLM agents. Existing prompt-based defenses offer limited protection, prompting the proposal of a reasoning-driven defense prompt and an experience-based defense called ToolShield, which provides more durable protection over sustained interactions. The study highlights the need for defenses that consider entire action sequences and their cumulative effects rather than isolated prompts or responses.

item.title: Researchers identify 'Less is Less' effect where sparse-attention algorithms increase sequence length and complexity in large language model decoding [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers have found that applying post-training sparse-attention algorithms during the decode stage of large language model inference can paradoxically increase overall complexity by causing longer output sequences, a phenomenon they call "Less is Less" (Lil). This challenges prior assumptions that sparse attention reduces latency and memory use in decoding, which typically dominates inference time. To address this, the team proposes an early-stopping algorithm that detects when information loss from sparse attention outweighs its benefits, effectively reducing token consumption by up to 90% with less than 2% accuracy loss on reasoning-intensive benchmarks. Their work combines empirical and theoretical analysis to highlight trade-offs in sparse decoding and offers a practical method to improve efficiency without significant performance degradation.

item.title: GradAlign introduces gradient-aligned data selection for LLM reinforcement learning to improve training stability and performance across challenging data regimes [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: GradAlign is a new method for selecting training data in reinforcement learning (RL) for large language models (LLMs) that uses a small trusted validation set to prioritize problems whose policy gradients align with validation gradients, creating an adaptive curriculum. This approach addresses the sensitivity of RL to training problem quality caused by non-stationary policies and exploration, which differs from supervised fine-tuning. The method was evaluated on scenarios with unreliable rewards, distribution imbalance, and low-utility training data, consistently outperforming existing baselines and demonstrating more stable training and better final results. The implementation of GradAlign is publicly available on GitHub.

item.title: Researchers propose HiCI hierarchical attention module to extend LLaMA-2 context length up to 100K tokens with under 5.5% parameter increase [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers introduce HiCI (Hierarchical Construction-Integration), a hierarchical attention module inspired by cognitive theories, that builds segment-level representations and integrates them into a global context to improve long-context language modeling. They adapt LLaMA-2 models with less than 5.5% additional parameters, extending context windows from 4K to 100K tokens for the 7B model and 64K tokens for the 13B model. HiCI shows consistent performance gains across language modeling, retrieval, and instruction-following benchmarks, matching proprietary models on topic retrieval and outperforming GPT-3.5-Turbo-16K on code comprehension tasks. These results highlight the benefit of explicit hierarchical structuring as an inductive bias for handling long contexts in language models.

item.title: Researchers find that lossy memory in language models can be more harmful than no memory when it retains incorrect conclusions without their derivation, proposing a source-first compression policy to improve correctability [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A study shows that language models with lossy memory that preserves wrong conclusions but not the underlying reasoning can confidently repeat errors, whereas empty memory leads to abstention. This brittle memory effect depends on whether the memory retains the re-derivation basis rather than just the answer. The researchers introduce reclaim evaluation, a method that induces known errors, compresses memory at a fixed budget, applies corrections, and measures exact recovery without human judgment. They demonstrate that keeping the recomputable source and dropping the re-derivable conclusion restores correctability at equal memory size, and they validate these findings across multiple deployed memory systems, real dialogue datasets, and agent benchmarks. The team also releases tools and validators to support further research on memory compression and error correction in language models.

item.title: Researchers release MTEB-PT, a Portuguese benchmark evaluating 17 sentence embedding models across 14 datasets for tasks including similarity, classification, retrieval, and reranking [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Portuguese remains underrepresented in text embedding evaluations despite its global prevalence, leading to reliance on English or multilingual metrics that may not reflect Portuguese-specific performance. Researchers introduced MTEB-PT, a benchmark derived from 14 datasets covering semantic textual similarity, classification, retrieval, and reranking, to assess 17 open- and closed-source embedding models under a unified protocol. Their findings reveal that model performance in Portuguese varies significantly by task, with no single model excelling universally and models with stronger long-context capabilities performing better on longer inputs. The study also demonstrates that language-specific fine-tuning enhances model effectiveness in Portuguese, particularly when the fine-tuning data aligns closely with the target task. To explore this, three backbone models were fine-tuned using Portuguese contrastive supervision and Matryoshka Representation Learning, yielding notable improvements in semantic textual similarity and retrieval tasks while maintaining competitiveness under dimensional truncation. The researchers have made the MTEB-PT benchmark, fine-tuned models, and associated training and evaluation code publicly available.

item.title: Researchers develop a 146M-parameter language model auditor that detects behavioural faithfulness gaps missed by human raters and frontier zero-shot judges [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers have created a small, purpose-built 146-million-parameter language model auditor that detects behavioural faithfulness issues such as sycophancy, dependence, and confabulated memories in generator models unseen during training. This auditor outperforms independent human raters, who show low agreement, and a frontier zero-shot judge, achieving an AUROC of 0.804 compared to 0.721 for the judge, and maintains performance across diverse model families where human judgement falls to chance. The auditor uses a hyperbolic substrate and a linear read-out of frozen representations, with hierarchical benefits demonstrated through ablation studies comparing it to Euclidean controls on multi-domain structures. This approach suggests that measuring behavioural faithfulness in language models is more effective with specialized small instruments rather than relying on scale or human evaluation alone.

item.title: Researchers analyze bidirectional induction mechanisms in masked diffusion language models, revealing symmetric context use and implicit timestep computation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: This study examines how masked diffusion language models (DLMs) implement induction, a key mechanism for in-context learning where the model identifies repeated contexts and copies subsequent tokens. Comparing DLMs with autoregressive (AR) transformers of similar architecture, the researchers find that DLMs develop a bidirectional induction circuit that operates symmetrically on past and future context, unlike AR models which only access left context. The DLMs show stronger induction capabilities when both sides of a masked token are visible, indicating bidirectional context access rather than enhanced one-sided processing. Beyond induction, the analysis provides causal evidence that DLMs estimate the global fraction of masked tokens and use this as an implicit timestep signal, despite lacking explicit timestep embeddings. This insight advances understanding of the internal mechanisms of diffusion-based language models, an emerging alternative to autoregressive transformers for text generation through iterative denoising.

item.title: Bloomy launches AI-powered mastery learning platform for K-12, offering personalized skill diagnostics and Socratic tutoring to improve student outcomes [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Bloomy, a startup from Y Combinator S26, has launched an AI-driven mastery learning platform for K-12 students that diagnoses skill gaps and creates personalized learning paths. The platform integrates third-party assessments and uses a Socratic AI tutor to guide students through lessons without giving away answers, aiming to replicate the benefits of one-on-one tutoring at scale. The system adapts to each student's performance, requiring 90% mastery before advancing and providing scaffolded support through a digital tutor called BloomyBot. The AI tutor is designed to stay on topic, avoid giving direct answers, and support multiple languages. Bloomy emphasizes that its AI is not a replacement for human teachers but a tool to enhance personalized instruction and address learning gaps more precisely.

item.title: Survey reviews GNN-based link prediction techniques and applications, proposing a taxonomy of architectures and highlighting challenges and future directions [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: A recent survey paper provides a comprehensive review of Graph Neural Network (GNN)-based link prediction methods, introducing a taxonomy that categorizes advancements by techniques and applications. It focuses on key GNN architectures such as GCN, GAE, GAT, and GFormer, discussing their strengths and limitations. The paper also highlights practical applications in knowledge graphs and recommendation systems, examines current challenges, and suggests promising future research directions.

item.title: Researchers introduce masked diffusion language models as steerable text-based world models for agentic reinforcement learning, showing improved coherence and diversity over larger autoregressive models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers propose masked diffusion language models (MDLMs) as text-based world models for reinforcement learning (RL), addressing limitations of autoregressive models in conditioning on globally interdependent state anchors. They formalize world modeling as a steerable transition-dynamics problem and curate a large dataset of grounded state-action trajectories across multiple environments and model families. The study compares MDLMs with autoregressive language models, demonstrating that MDLMs achieve better coherence, groundedness, and rollout diversity at comparable inference latency despite smaller parameter sizes. Using a plug-and-play GRPO training framework, the researchers perform zero-shot transfer tests on out-of-distribution environments with various agent backbones, achieving up to 47% absolute gains over baselines without environment-specific fine-tuning. They also analyze failure modes under adversarial conditions and conduct human evaluations on realism and training utility, releasing their work to support further research in this area.

item.title: Researchers evaluate late-interaction multi-vector scoring for graph-linked image retrieval in multimodal question answering, showing improved accuracy on MultimodalQA dataset [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers propose replacing single-vector bi-encoder similarity with late-interaction MaxSim-style multi-vector scoring for ranking graph-linked image nodes in multimodal question answering systems. This approach maintains existing offline graph construction, text and table retrieval, and downstream reasoning while improving retrieval accuracy for visual evidence. Evaluation on the MultimodalQA dataset shows gains in retrieval-stage performance and downstream question answering, particularly where visual evidence is critical, though results vary for text-dominant questions. The study highlights the importance of fine-grained visual alignment and suggests further validation and detailed graph-level analysis are needed.

item.title: RAIL Guard introduces a closed-loop pipeline to evaluate and remediate LLM outputs across eight dimensions, improving convergence rates over block-and-retry methods [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: RAIL Guard is a responsible AI system for large language model agents that moves beyond binary blocking of unsafe content by evaluating outputs on eight measurable dimensions and iteratively remediating failures through an evaluate-rewrite-reevaluate loop. Tested on four leading LLMs with thousands of outputs and agent tool-call scenarios, it achieved 96.9% convergence compared to 49.1% for traditional block-and-retry, with feedback-driven self-repair reaching 86.6% convergence on fixable issues without significant utility loss. The system also reduces unsafe agent executions by 33% through pre-tool-call evaluation without affecting task completion and distinguishes between fixable dimensions and structural issues requiring architectural solutions. RAIL Guard is available as open-source SDKs.

item.title: Researchers propose a language-centric framework expressing multimodal data as atomic propositions unified by a global semantic codebook for interpretable, compositional understanding [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers propose a language representation framework for multimodal data where observations from images, videos, or text are expressed as bags of atomic propositions-simple statements about entities, actions, and relations. A global semantic codebook unifies these propositions into a shared vocabulary, creating an interpretable space that spans fine-grained facts to high-level concepts and enables compositional reasoning and cross-modal understanding. The framework supports complex multimodal understanding, rich data curation, and structured retrieval, demonstrated on autonomous driving and open-world datasets. This approach aims to enhance interpretability and reasoning across different data modalities by placing them into a common semantic space.

item.title: Researchers formalize Exact Network Surgery for bit-exact in-place insertion of residual blocks preserving network function and trainability in live computational graphs [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers introduce Exact Network Surgery, a method for inserting residual blocks into live computational graphs that preserves the network's function bit-exactly under floating-point assumptions and allows immediate training of inserted parameters. They prove key theorems on identity morphism, structural locality, and gradient behavior, and identify a degenerate configuration that acts as a saddle point preventing gradient descent escape. The approach is validated using NeuroDSL, a reactive graph engine in Julia, demonstrating bit-exact grafting, predictable gradient dynamics, consistent training resumption after process restarts, and efficient computation tied to the downstream cone size.

item.title: DS@GT develops hybrid multi-agent LLM system for conversational depression screening, ranking 2nd at eRisk 2026 with cost-effective open-source model [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: DS@GT submitted a hybrid multi-agent large language model system to the eRisk 2026 Task 1 challenge, designed for conversational depression screening by interviewing simulated personas and estimating Beck Depression Inventory II scores without direct sensitive questions. Their system evolved from a single-model prototype to a multi-agent architecture and finally to a hybrid model combining a paid GPT-5-nano interviewer with the open-source Gemma 27B, enhanced by algorithmic components to improve reasoning and reliability. The hybrid system was tested on 20 personas with three automated runs, achieving a top ADODL score of 0.9063 that placed DS@GT second among 21 teams and outperformed their paid baseline at roughly one-quarter of the API cost per persona. These results suggest that with sufficient algorithmic guidance, weaker open-source models can effectively compete with stronger proprietary models in conversational interviewing tasks. DS@GT has made their source code publicly available for further research and development.

item.title: Researchers introduce C-MTP, a faster direct supervision method for training continuous Chain-of-Thought models that outperforms prior approaches on short reasoning traces but struggles with longer, complex tasks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers propose C-MTP, a simpler and faster direct supervision technique for continuous Chain-of-Thought (CoT) models that models each latent representation as an average of embeddings from CoT traces. This method outperforms previous direct supervision approaches and performs competitively with slower indirect supervision methods on tasks with simplified CoT traces under 100 tokens. The study extends evaluation to more complex tasks with reasoning traces of several hundred tokens, finding that both direct and indirect supervision methods experience about a 65% performance drop, highlighting current limitations of continuous CoT models. The researchers have released their code and checkpoints publicly.

item.title: PriorProof introduces a time-relative metric for technique novelty in formal Lean proofs using dependency footprints and prior snapshots of Mathlib [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: PriorProof is a method to measure the novelty of formal proofs in Lean by analyzing the dependency footprint of proof terms against a prior snapshot of Mathlib, without requiring human labels or predefined technique ontologies. It scores proofs based on weighted surprisal under a retrieval-conditioned prior and was evaluated in a blinded topology study comparing its judgments to expert raters. In the study, PriorProof agreed with domain experts on about 70% of 76 proof pairs, including 92% agreement on canonical contrasts, and showed comparable performance to a language model baseline. The method provides a decomposable, time-anchored signal with an interpretable reliability indicator, intended to complement rather than replace expert or model judgments in assessing proof novelty.

item.title: Researchers present device-agnostic speculative decoding implementation for large language models, achieving up to 1.61× speedup on Apple silicon with verified output distribution [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers developed a device-agnostic implementation of speculative decoding for large language models, which uses a small draft model to propose multiple tokens and a target model to score them in batch, preserving output distribution. Their empirical study on a consumer Apple-silicon laptop verified distribution equivalence and found the best configuration achieved a 1.61× wall-clock speedup at six tokens, though some configurations slowed down due to hardware and model limitations. The study highlights that speculative decoding benefits depend on genuine batch-parallel verification and a significant latency gap between draft and target models.

item.title: Researchers develop self-modifying Lean proof agents with verifier-grounded coevolving benchmarks, achieving 45.1% solve rate on held-out tests [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers present a self-evolving Lean proof agent that coevolves both the agent and its benchmark within a Lean-grounded verification loop, ensuring all proofs are machine-verified. The system uses a mastery-throttled curriculum to introduce harder proof tasks only after mastering current levels, maintaining score comparability through recalibration. Over 15 generations, the coevolving agent outperformed fixed-benchmark baselines, reaching a 45.1% solve rate on a held-out miniF2F test split compared to 12.7% for the seed and 32.0% for the best fixed-benchmark agent, demonstrating that verifier-grounded self-evolution can improve formal proof workflows.

item.title: Researchers derive and validate a formal law predicting performance uplift from diversity in Large Language Model ensembles across multiple benchmarks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: This paper presents a formally derived and experimentally validated law for quantifying the performance uplift that diversity of thought provides in ensembles of Large Language Models (LLMs). The authors decompose ensemble lift into rescue and damage components and develop a heuristic based on an accuracy-adjusted correctness correlation, accuracy gap, and collective accuracy to predict ensemble performance. They test this law on over 767,000 inferences from ten open-weight models across graduate-level science benchmarks and a novel cybersecurity benchmark involving multi-turn digital-forensics tasks.

item.title: Panache introduces a one-pass streaming algorithm for z-normalized pan matrix profile motif discovery, achieving near-linear runtime and outperforming CPU and GPU baselines on large time series datasets [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Panache is a new algorithm designed for motif discovery in time series data, addressing the challenge of unknown pattern durations by scanning all window lengths in a single pass. Unlike existing methods that perform multiple quadratic self-joins for each length, Panache uses a spectral approach with sliding-DFT recurrences and hashing to efficiently identify recurring patterns with near-linear runtime. The algorithm automatically computes data-dependent parameters and requires only a resource budget to tune. In benchmarks on 17 UCR datasets, Panache recovered all top-20 motifs compared to exact ground truth and outperformed all tested CPU and GPU baselines. On a large Wafer dataset with five million samples over 51 lengths, Panache completed motif discovery in 6 minutes, significantly faster than the fastest exact CPU method and SCAMP on an H100 GPU.

item.title: Researchers present FluxBench to benchmark AI agent performance on end-to-end RTL-to-GDS electronic design automation workflows, revealing significant efficiency and capability differences [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Researchers introduce FluxBench, a systematic evaluation framework for AI agents across complete electronic design automation (EDA) workflows, including RTL generation and RTL-to-GDS flows using both open-source and commercial tools. The study assesses agents' abilities in code generation, iterative repair, tool feedback utilization, logic synthesis, placement and routing, and engineering change order automation, while introducing Token ROI as a metric for cost-efficiency relative to token usage and runtime. Experimental results show that agent system architectures built on the same foundation model can differ in performance by up to 86.27%, with Token ROI varying by as much as 105.92 times among similarly performing systems. In a case study using the PicoRV32 design, the FluxEDA agent achieved an end-to-end score of 97.94, outperforming Claude Code with domain-specific EDA skills by up to 8.39 times, indicating that domain-specific skills alone do not guarantee improved performance in large-scale EDA tasks. The findings highlight the importance of both agent system design and foundation model capabilities in enabling effective automated EDA workflows.

item.title: Researchers identify curvature shadow as artifact causing apparent failure in maximum-entropy equilibrium selection in Kuhn poker [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers analyzed the apparent discrepancy in maximum-entropy equilibrium selection by Regularized Nash Dynamics (R-NaD) in Kuhn poker, where a small coordinate gap was observed compared to the theoretical maximum-entropy solution. They demonstrated that this gap arises from a curvature shadow effect linked to a minor, removable entropy shortfall on a flat entropy peak, rather than a genuine selection bias. The study quantified the relationship between the gap, entropy shortfall, and curvature across multiple games, confirming that the maximum-entropy selection holds except for this curvature-limited residual in sequential games like Kuhn poker.

item.title: ZifaMem introduces structured memory system for AI companions to improve persona, preference, and emotional continuity, boosting emotional-intelligence scores by 11.4% across multiple models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: ZifaMem is a structured memory system designed to enhance AI companions' ability to maintain emotional continuity by organizing dialogue into session summaries, episodic memories, and a consolidated user model. It improves emotional-intelligence scores by 11.4% compared to using full raw dialogue history and shows significant gains in persona grounding across multiple AI backbones, including a 42% relative improvement with Claude. The system was evaluated under a fixed large language model judging protocol with route audits, demonstrating a 39% net preference for multi-turn affect context over single-turn snapshots. Three memory systems, including ZifaMem, Mem0, and filtered verbatim retrieval, each significantly outperformed raw-history deployment, with ZifaMem and Mem0 showing statistical equivalence on primary preference endpoints. The ZifaMem SDK, CLI, and portable Agent Skills have been open-sourced for broader use.

item.title: Researchers run first controlled study on progressive disclosure for long-context AI agents, finding one-level disclosure effective for large corpora [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Researchers conducted the first controlled study comparing progressive disclosure-a method where AI agents access only necessary document parts-to raw-document navigation and hybrid retrievers for long-document question answering. They tested various agent designs and model families on InfiniteBench, focusing on tasks ranging from single books to multiple books. The study found that progressive disclosure improves performance when agents struggle with raw navigation and scales better for large corpora, while adding deeper routing levels can reduce accuracy. The approach enhances context management rather than agent intelligence, proving beneficial when the document set is too large for direct reading.

item.title: PAMD: Structured Adaptive Distances for Bisimulation Representations in Visual Reinforcement Learning [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.18004v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Many visual reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms learn representations by matching latent distances to a behavioral distance induced by reward and transition similarity. In practice, the choice of the latent distance can strongly affect performance: using a fixed, pre-specified global norms (e.g., $\ell_p$ norms or other hand-designed metrics) may be overly restrictive to capture the behavioral distance. In contrast, unconstrained pairwise distances may admit degenerate solutions that drive the metric loss down without improving the representation. To address this gap, we introduce **PAMD: Pairwise Adaptive Mahalanobis Distance**, which parameterizes a positive-definite, pair-conditioned metric for measuring latent state similarity. PAMD is a simple plug-in for existing bisimulation-based methods, offering a more expressive yet structured alternative to fixed, pre-specified latent distances. We empirically validate our method on visual MuJoCo continuous-control tasks, where final performance of several recent bisimulation-based RL algorithms is substantially improved when equipped with the distance we propose.

item.title: Logical Judgments Under Pressure: Diagnosing Syllogistic Stability with Learned Soft Prefixes [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.18228v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: To test how correct logical judgments respond to learned context, we prepend a soft prefix to an exactly labeled syllogistic reasoning benchmark while keeping the model fixed. Soft prefixes are opaque continuous vectors, so we characterize them through the behavior they induce across controlled variations in logical form and interface. By studying which prefixes succeed and how their effects generalize, we characterize how learned contextual pressure can override correct judgments and expose limits in a model's logical stability. Across Qwen3.6-35B-A3B MoE, Qwen3-8B, and Gemma 4 31B, learned prefixes redirect many correct answers and remain effective across unseen forms and interface changes. In repeated tests with Qwen3.6 MoE and Gemma, they outperform paired random controls in all 16 model--direction--split comparisons by 37 to 99 percentage points. Qwen3.6 MoE flip rates remain between 72% and 90% across wording and prompt changes, while Gemma validity prefixes retain 54% to 56% flip compared with less than 1% for matched random prefixes. Diagnostic tests show that the dominant effect is a broad preference for one answer meaning rather than fixed-symbol forcing or a logical operation that transfers reliably between tasks. The form of this bias differs across models. In both Qwen models, simple score models often predict which judgments will flip but not how far their margins will move, whereas Gemma's overall response is more closely approximated by the same models. These results show that the dominant behavioral effect of successful soft prefixes is a broad answer preference, while the remaining response reveals substantial model-specific differences in logical stability.

item.title: Comparing Spectrogram Front-Ends for Abnormal Heart-Sound Detection with a Convolutional Neural Network [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.16220v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Heart disease kills a lot of people, and one cheap way to catch it early is by listening to heart sounds with a stethoscope, or better yet, just recording them and running them through a model. This project is a binary classification task: take a short clip of someones heartbeat and decide if it sounds normal or abnormal. Instead of trying out a bunch of different models, we kept the CNN the same the whole time and just changed how we turned the raw audio into a picture for it to look at. We tried three ways of doing that: a regular logmel spectrogram, PCEN (which basically normalizes each frequency bin over time), and a multi resolution version that stacks a few different window sizes together. We ran all three on the PhysioNet 2016 heart-sound dataset with the exact same setup but same model, same optimizer, same random seed. Turns out all three do pretty well at catching abnormal cases (sensitivity around 0.95), but PCEN and multi-resolution both edge out the plain logmel on the official PhysioNet accuracy metric (0.915 and 0.916 vs. 0.910). We also ran Grad-CAM to see where the model was actually looking, and it mostly focused on the low frequencies where S1 and S2 heart sounds live, which is a good sign that it learned something real

item.title: Fully-sensorized smart-eyewear platform for on-device Machine Learning [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.16222v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper presents ARGO, a smart eyewear platform designed to bridge ergonomic comfort, high computational throughput, and energy efficiency. Unlike cloud-dependent solutions, ARGO leverages the STM32N6 microcontroller and its integrated Neural Processing Unit (NPU) to enable on-device machine learning, minimizing latency and preserving user privacy through local data processing. The primary contribution lies in the holistic co-design of hardware, firmware, and artificial intelligence, centered on the deployment of an optimized YOLOv11 model for real-time urban obstacle recognition. To ensure compatibility with the target NPU, we introduce Head-wise Parallel Attention (HPA), an architectural refinement that enables efficient accelerator execution while preserving the original computational logic. The model is trained on the Walking On The Road (WOTR) dataset, and the final deployed configuration achieves an mAP50-95 of 24 under strict memory constraints, with a memory footprint of only 2.483 MB. The platform integrates a multimodal sensor suite, RGB cameras, Time-of-Flight sensors, microphones, and ambient sensors, and delivers 10 FPS at a continuous autonomy of ~113 minutes on a 200 mAh battery. These results demonstrate the feasibility of a high-performance, privacy-preserving, and socially acceptable assistive device, and highlight how competitive edge AI solutions increasingly demand tightly integrated, multidisciplinary co-design approaches.

item.title: RouteCost: A Production-Inspired Multi-Stage Framework for Pre-Order Shipping Cost Estimation in E-Commerce [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.16230v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate pre-order shipping cost estimation is important in e-commerce because it affects price presentation, margin planning, and conversion. In practice, shipping cost is shaped not only by distance but also by destination demand mix, billable weight, dimensional pricing, surcharge triggers, and latent operational effects such as shipment consolidation. Static lookup methods therefore miss important sources of variation, while monolithic regressors may exploit strong but non-causal correlations. We propose RouteCost, a production-inspired multi-stage framework that decomposes the problem into time-aware demand forecasting, fee-card-informed baseline pricing, Stage 2 residual correction, and proxy-based box-consolidation inference. Route-level cost estimates are aggregated through a route-weighted expectation formulation to produce product-level shipping cost predictions. Across over 250,000 orders, 260 products, and 18 months of order history, the framework improves predictive quality and aggregate calibration while preserving route-level interpretability.

item.title: Token-Level Cross-Modal Transformer with Contrastive Multi-Task Learning for Breast Cancer Subtype Classification and Survival Prediction [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.16233v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Integrating heterogeneous genomic and clinical modalities for joint cancer subtype classification and survival prediction remains a key challenge in precision oncology. Existing approaches suffer from three limitations: (1) they treat each modality as a monolithic feature vector, precluding fine-grained token-level interactions across modalities; (2) cross-modal fusion is typically performed through linear weighting or late averaging rather than structured token exchange; and (3) survival and classification objectives are optimized independently, missing a joint regularization signal.

item.title: HantaWatch: Federated Learning for Hantavirus Genomic Surveillance [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.16234v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Hantavirus genomic surveillance is limited by the distribution of sequence data, non-IID source heterogeneity, and constrained expert-review capacity. We propose HantaWatch, a federated learning framework that enables laboratories and surveillance sites to collaboratively train sequence-based models without sharing raw data. HantaWatch integrates k-mer feature extraction, source-aware federated client construction, adaptive DU-FedProx optimization, surveillance-specific model selection, and prediction-only triage. Experiments on binary and multi-class tasks show that HantaWatch supports high-risk screening, outbreak-associated prediction, clade classification, and clinical-syndrome categorization while balancing predictive performance, false-negative risk, and update stability. The framework converts model output into risk scores, confidence estimates, uncertainty flags, and ranked expert-review priorities. HantaWatch therefore provides a practical federated decision-support layer for decentralized Hantavirus surveillance, supporting expert prioritization without replacing laboratory or public-health interpretation.

item.title: OpenMHC: Accelerating the Science of Wearable Foundation Models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.16235v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Mobile and wearable devices offer an unprecedented opportunity for continuous, passive health monitoring and active health coaching. However, the largest wearable datasets are not publicly available for research, and leading wearable foundation models trained on such datasets are rarely open-weight or come with reproducible training code. To accelerate open science in wearable health, we release OpenMyHeartCounts (OpenMHC), the largest and most comprehensive open-access wearable health dataset to date, alongside open-source implementations of recent wearable foundation models. OpenMHC, derived from over a decade of data collected through the My Heart Counts study app, includes >60 million hours of wearable data across 19 sensor channels (e.g., step count, heart rate, sleep, workouts) and up to 169 linked variables, including health, lifestyle, mood, and behavior from 11,894 consenting participants. Furthermore, we introduce a unified, open benchmark that enables standardized comparison of wearable health models across three tracks: health and behavior downstream prediction, multivariate data imputation, and time-series forecasting. We benchmark classical methods alongside recent wearable and multivariate time series foundation models. By open-sourcing data, code, and model weights at this unprecedented scale, we aim to democratize wearable health AI research and enable the community to drive open progress in this domain.

item.title: The Failures of Marginal Influence-Based Attribution Methods for Global Time Series Explanations [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.16236v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Explainability methods for time series models predominantly produce flat attribution scores: they quantify the direct influence of a feature at a timestamp by a scalar. We prove that the dominant failure mode of such methods is not the scalar format itself but a fundamental computational mismatch: existing methods compute scores via marginal conditioning or off-manifold gradients, both of which conflate direct temporal dependencies with mediated ones under autocorrelation. We also define DAG-faithfulness: an explanation is DAG-faithful if the temporal dependency graph it encodes is Markov-equivalent to the temporal directed acyclic graph (DAG) implicitly learned by the model. Particularly, we observe that standard attribution methods, specifically SHAP, are not DAG-faithful in general, and that recent time-series-aware extensions inherit the same computational limitation.

item.title: Quantizing Recursive Reasoning Models [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.16237v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recursive reasoning models solve hard puzzles by applying compact, weight-tied blocks over many refinement steps. Because these blocks are reused many times, quantizing them creates a unique dynamical problem: the quantization error is incurred at every step. While 8-bit quantization (integer or float) preserves accuracy, moving to a per-tensor 4-bit format causes a systematic bias to accumulate. The ensuing drift catastrophically degrades exact-solution accuracy on Sudoku from 84.1% to 0.0% (only ~25% of cells correct). In this work, we show that this collapse is caused by activation-scaling granularity rather than bit-width or number format. Crucially, moving to per-block scaling completely restores the transition. To implement this, we apply MXInt4, a blockwise integer activation format, to recursive reasoning models. It is competitive with blockwise float formats on our tasks, while keeping integer elements and power-of-two block scales. Finally, recursion depth and reuse modulate quantization sensitivity, with the deepest architecture we test (the EqR equilibrium model) the most sensitive. Yet blockwise scaling overcomes this vulnerability, staying robust across these architectures and transferring to the open-ended ARC-AGI benchmark.

item.title: Diffusion-corrected Autoregressive Fourier Neural Operator for Droplet Evolution Prediction [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.16238v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Predicting droplet evolution in material jetting, or Inkjet Printing (IJP), is essential for maintaining printing quality. However, long-horizon forecasts remain challenging due to error accumulation and the complex coupling of process variables. In this work, we introduce the Diffusion-corrected Auto-Regressive Fourier Neural Operator (DiffARFNO), a two-stage framework that combines an autoregressive Fourier-MIONet with a conditional Denoising Diffusion Implicit Model (DDIM) corrector. Fourier-MIONet is trained as a coarse predictor and deployed autoregressively for long-horizon forecasting. In the second stage, a DDIM-based conditional corrector refines the coarse prediction within each sliding window through efficient iterative denoising. By combining coarse predictions from Fourier-MIONet with a DDIM corrector that restores fine details, DiffARFNO aims to provide high-fidelity predictions for long-horizon forecasts. Extensive experiments on droplet datasets from ANSYS Fluent demonstrate that DiffARFNO significantly outperforms existing state-of-the-art models.

item.title: Normalized Rewards for Preference Optimization [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.16240v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Direct Alignment Algorithms (DAAs) such as DPO have become a common way to post-train and align LLMs with human preferences. However, DAAs have been observed to over-optimize their implicit reward model and decrease the likelihood of preferred responses. This results in a decrease in the total likelihood assigned to responses seen in the preference dataset, potentially resulting in undesirable behavior. To counteract this undesired side-effect of DAAs, we examine the effect of using objectives that add a regularization term to maintain the total length-normalized probabilities of the chosen and rejected responses. To better understand over-optimization, we investigate how response likelihood changes are distributed over the tokens with and without regularization. We find that a significant portion of the likelihood changes are due to a small set of outlier tokens, which explains how DAAs improve generation quality despite decreasing the likelihoods of chosen responses. We apply the proposed regularization to reference-based (DPO) and reference-free (SimPO) methods and find (1) improved trade-offs between generation quality and general benchmark capability and (2) improvements in reward modeling across datasets. For example, on Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct, we see both a >20% relative increase in AlpacaEval2 scores and >9% relative performance gains on general benchmarks. Additionally, we find that the added regularization term effectively mitigates the amount of displacement within preferred responses overall, and for the outlier tokens specifically, by utilizing low-likelihood tokens.

item.title: KernelBench-Verified: Do LLM-Generated Kernels Actually Beat PyTorch? [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.16241v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent large language models (LLMs) can generate custom CUDA kernels that appear to outperform PyTorch on benchmarks such as KernelBench. Building upon this foundational framework, we demonstrate that frontier models frequently engage in reward hacking to artificially inflate reported performance. In this work, we identify two areas where evaluation frameworks must co-evolve with model capabilities. First, to accurately measure true speedup, we examine the baseline timing mechanism, noting that enabling Tensor Core acceleration with TF32 provides a more realistic estimation of execution on modern GPUs. Second, concerning algorithmic correctness, models often exploit the narrow test distribution by hardcoding bypasses for specific tensor values. By skipping required computations, these kernels artificially accelerate execution rather than implementing actual CUDA kernels. We introduce KernelBench-Verified, an extended evaluation framework that incorporates a TF32-enabled baseline and a four-distribution hidden test suite. We additionally introduce memory efficiency metrics that capture the often-overlooked speed-memory tradeoff in kernel optimization. Under verified single-turn evaluation with seven frontier LLMs, we find that the best-performing model (GPT-5.5) achieves a 0.88x geometric mean speedup, significantly lower than the 1.43x speedup observed under the standard evaluation protocol. No model consistently outperforms PyTorch when evaluated against realistic baselines. On the memory front, 28% of GPU kernels generated by the best model increase peak GPU memory usage. Our findings demonstrate the necessity of continually adapting robust evaluation protocols as LLM kernel generation capabilities advance.

item.title: TRACE: Trajectory-Based Safety Patch Learning for LLM Post-Training Realignment [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.16242v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fine-Tuning-as-a-Service (FTaaS) platforms let users train large language models (LLMs) on customized tasks, but this pipeline could erode models' safety alignment. In practice, service providers need to recover models' safety without re-running full alignment, or destroying the utility gained from customized tasks. A line of existing work refers to model parameter merging, which adds a safety patch on the fine-tuned model parameters to shift the model away from unsafe tendencies. However, this merging-based paradigm is fundamentally bottlenecked by task-safety update entanglement: downstream task updates and the safety patch often overlap in their dominant directions, so the merge strength is intrinsically hard to calibrate. If the safety vector is scaled too weakly, harmful components could still dominate, preventing the model from returning to a safe region; if it is scaled too aggressively, it suppresses task-relevant directions and degrades utility. To solve this problem, we shift the focus of merging-based methods from designing online merging operators to offline patch learning, and seek a safety patch that minimally interferes with task-relevant directions while retaining decisive control over unsafe behaviors. We propose TRACE, a trajectory-based safety patch learning framework that (i) simulates harmful tuning trajectories to generate progressively corrupted states, and (ii) optimizes a plug-in patch to recover safety while maintaining utility across varying corrupted base states. Across six benchmarks and two models, TRACE consistently dominates the safety-utility frontier. TRACE reaches nearly 100% safety on all settings, while maintaining comparable utility to the undefended fine-tuned model.

item.title: RobustMAD: Evaluating Real-World Robustness of Multimodal Small Language Models for Deployable Anomaly Detection Assistants [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.16243v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Multimodal industrial anomaly inspection assistants are a critical component of next-generation smart factories, enabling interactive vision-language-based querying. However, multimodal large language models remain impractical for on-site deployment due to prohibitive computational demands and privacy risks from cloud-based inference. Compact multimodal small language models (MSLMs) offer a deployable alternative, yet progress is constrained by the lack of comprehensive robustness analyses and meaningfully challenging benchmarks that reflect real-world industrial conditions. To address this gap, we develop RobustMAD, the first deployment-motivated benchmark, designed to comprehensively evaluate model robustness through diverse open-ended queries spanning object understanding, anomaly detection, unanswerable problems, and visual quality degradations. Contrary to conventional assumptions, top-performing MSLMs exhibit promising capabilities, surprisingly outperforming even the larger GPT-5 Nano. However, they still fall short of safety-critical requirements, and RobustMAD reveals critical robustness gaps that pose operational risks. In particular, three recurring failure modes emerge: (i) fragile multimodal grounding under fine-grained distinctions or degraded visual conditions, (ii) insufficiently comprehensive responses, and (iii) weak logical grounding on unanswerable or ill-posed queries, leading to hallucinated outputs. Grounded in these insights, we provide actionable guidance for the design of next-generation multimodal industrial inspection assistants that leverage their promising competence. Code is available at https://github.com/en-research/RobustMAD.

item.title: Learning Structural Manipulability in Gate-Level Netlists Using Graph Neural Networks [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.16245v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gate-level netlists exhibit intrinsic structural properties that influence signal propagation independently of functional simulation. We define a topology-driven structural manipulability score that characterizes node-level structural flexibility using path participation, k-core embedding, symmetry, and centrality. Modeling netlists as directed graphs, we formulate node-level regression to learn this topology-derived score using graph neural networks (GNNs). Experiments on ISCAS85 and EPFL benchmarks evaluate how effectively different GNN architectures approximate this metric across held-out circuits, with hierarchical models yielding the most consistent rankings. Component-level and ablation analyses examine the contribution of individual factors. As an illustrative case study, analysis of Trojan-injected circuits using TrustHub templates reveals statistically distinguishable structural patterns, indicating that topology-based scoring provides complementary structural insight.

item.title: Let the Data Decide: Supervision Analysis, Capability Trade-offs, and Adaptive Objective Routing in Continued Pre-Training via Off-Policy Distillation [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.16246v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Off-policy distillation is now central to large language model pre-training, yet how training data, objective parameterization, and model capabilities interact remains poorly characterized. We studies top-$k$-truncated, temperature-scaled off-policy distillation by decomposing this problem into two questions: an \emph{objective-to-capability} analysis of how the training objective shapes token-level supervision and downstream performance, and a \emph{data-to-objective} analysis of how data heterogeneity should inform objective routing. We first show that the language-modeling objective ($L_{\mathrm{LM}}$) and the knowledge-distillation objective ($L_{\mathrm{KD}}$) induce systematically different capability profiles, and trace this divergence to a gradient-level tension between \emph{direct observed-token reinforcement} and \emph{teacher-supported alternative supervision}. To quantify this tension, we introduce diagnostic metrics -- support coverage, observed-token probability mass, and teacher-distribution concentration -- and show via controlled sweeps that the support size $k$ governs a coverage-sharpness trade-off, while distillation temperature controls within-support probability allocation. We then examine adaptive objective routing: a domain-level policy that applies $L_{\mathrm{LM}}$ to math and code and $L_{\mathrm{KD}}$ to general-domain data yields consistent gains over both single-objective baselines, whereas token-level routing based on observed-token probability mass or teacher entropy fails to consistently match the single-objective baseline. These results suggest that effective objective routing depends less on routing granularity than on the quality of the routing signal, reframing continued pre-training via off-policy distillation as a structured, data-conditional supervision-design problem rather than a global hyperparameter choice.

item.title: High-accuracy Low-Bit KV-Cache Quantization via Local Distribution Restoration [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.16248v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Long-context large language model inference relies on the KV cache to avoid redundant attention computation, but incurs high memory and bandwidth overheads. Low-bit KV-cache quantization reduces this cost, yet it severely degrade quality; particularly, one-bit quantization reduces accuracy from 84.2% to 47.8% on Llama-3.1-8B under RULER. Rather than common beliefs that absolute error of logits, we find that the root cause is structured local misranking, where the distribution of logits in top-K region is drifted. We thereby propose local distribution restoration, a new technique that detects steps with high local distribution risk from quantized-logit features and restores only the selected top-K candidate distribution before token selection. We implement DGAP to achieve local distribution restoration, with efficient risk detcetors and correctors. Expeirments show that on Llama-3.1-8B, DGAP recovers K1V1 RULER accuracy from 47.8% to 83.2% and reduces distribution drift from 0.38 to 0.14; across Llama, Mistral, and Qwen models, it preserves the persistent low-bit KV-cache footprint with modest decode overhead.

item.title: Benchmarking Machine Learning Models for Multi-Omics-Based Breast Cancer Prediction [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: arXiv:2607.16250v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Estrogen Receptor (ER) status is a critical biomarker in breast cancer diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment selection. Recent advances in high-throughput sequencing technologies have enabled the generation of multi-omics datasets that provide complementary molecular information for computational prediction tasks. This study presents a systematic benchmarking analysis of classical machine learning models for ER status prediction using transcriptomic (RNA expression), genomic (copy number variation; CNV), and proteomic (RPPA) data from the TCGA-BRCA cohort. A rigorous experimental framework incorporating stratified train-test splitting, stratified five-fold cross-validation, class imbalance handling, and fold-specific feature selection was employed to ensure reliable evaluation and prevent data leakage. Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost, Support Vector Machines (SVM), and Logistic Regression were evaluated across single-omic and multi-omic settings. Results demonstrated that RNA expression provided the strongest predictive signal, while multi-omic integration yielded modest but consistent improvements over individual modalities. Among all evaluated approaches, Random Forest achieved the best overall performance in the integrated multi-omic setting, obtaining a balanced accuracy of 90.3\% and an ROC-AUC of 97.1\%. Furthermore, recurrent selection of biologically relevant genes, including \textit{ESR1}, \textit{PGR}, \textit{FOXA1}, and \textit{GATA3}, supported the biological validity of the learned models. These findings indicate that carefully regularized classical machine learning methods remain highly effective for small, high-dimensional genomic datasets and that multi-omic integration provides complementary information for breast cancer ER status prediction.

item.title: SOS-LoRA: Static Orthogonal-Subspace Low-Rank Adaptation with Fixed Multi-Scale Scaling [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
